item.subject: science
item.chapter_label: The night sky: Moon and calendars
item.stem:
Veena's school uses a solar calendar of 365 days most years, and adds one extra day every fourth year. Classmates mention the Earth, the Sun, the Moon, and the seasons.

Why is that leap day needed?

options.A: The Earth takes about 365¼ days to revolve around the Sun, so the spare quarter-days must be collected to keep the calendar aligned with the seasons.
options.B: The Moon takes extra days to orbit the Earth, so the solar calendar must add a day.
options.C: The calendar is lengthened so that the seasons will drift farther from the same dates each year.
options.D: The leap day is needed only as a school holiday and has no link to the Earth's motion around the Sun.
